Emma — thanks for the clear list. Attached are the items we can deliver today and a short summary of key controls. If you need additional context we can schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through next week.

Attachments (attached to this message):
- subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx (matrix: provider, service, residency, data types, delegated responsibilities)
- SOC2_Redwood_Inference_2025.pdf (redwood SOC 2 Type II report, redacted auditor appendix)
- redacted_CAIC_answers_2026.xlsx (CAIQ answers focused on encryption, keys, and data residency; redacted where necessary)

Executive summary (high level):
- KMS / keys: Redwood owns customer root keys in our KMS for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers may bring their own keys; we document ownership flow in the delegation matrix. EdgeScale should be scoped as a subprocessor only when explicitly enabled for model hosting or telemetry.
- Telemetry access: Our runtime emits aggregated telemetry to an internal metrics plane; we provide role-based access to partners for troubleshooting via short-lived credentials (ephemeral tokens) when approved. Any partner access is logged and recorded in audit logs; we provide a filtered view in compliance bundles.
- Onshore/residency: Most core infra providers are US/EU. We flag providers with APAC residency in the "residency" column of the matrix; these are subject to export-control review for regulated customers.
- Incident support & retention: Delegated responsibilities are mapped per provider. Our standard retention baseline is 30 days for runtime telemetry, 90 days for debug traces; customer-configured retention is possible for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm if the attached redactions are acceptable for your intake.
2) If you need original auditor evidence access rather than the redacted PDF, we can provide a controlled Drive link and an NDA-bound viewer role.
3) Let us know a time window to do a short technical walkthrough (we have availability Tue/Wed next week).

Regards,
